extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans and researchers of British television comedy
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic entry documenting the British sitcom The Inbetweeners, including production history, cast, episodes, reception, legacy and distribution details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: “Exquisitely accurate dialogue, capturing the feel of adolescence perfectly.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical praise singled out the dialogue as a key strength, implying that success relies on realistic, age-appropriate, and believable teen speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate portrayal of adolescence / male sixth-form experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme “captures the pathetic sixth-form male experience quite splendidly” and focuses on school life, male bonding, lad culture and adolescent sexuality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews contrast the show’s depiction of dull suburbia with more sensational teen dramas (e.g., Skins), suggesting a criterion of portraying ordinary, relatable adolescent experience rather than heightened fantasy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cringe and vulgar humour style
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre labels include coming-of-age, sex comedy, teen sitcom and cringe comedy; the series contains a “high quantity of strong language, crude humour and strong, frequent, sex references.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The show’s comedic voice depends on cringe situations, vulgarity and sexual themes; content choices affect certificate classifications (e.g., 18 certificate on DVDs, 15 theatrical for the film).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narration as framing device
rubrics_metrics.description: Will McKenzie is the central character, with his voiceover narrating each episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of a narrated central perspective is presented as structural/creative choice that shapes tone and audience alignment with the protagonist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble consistency and character focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The four main characters are seen in every episode as well as the films; character traits (e.g., Will the studious narrator, Simon the cynical one, Jay the vulgar liar, Neil the gullible gentle one) drive plots and humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining a stable core ensemble with clearly defined, contrasting personalities is presented as a hallmark of the show’s storytelling and comic dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic, suburban setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentators note the programme’s portrayal of dull suburbia is closer to the drab teen years most of us spent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grounded, recognisable setting (suburban school life) contributes to the series’ relatability and comedic effect; realism over glamorisation is implied as a quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural impact and quotability
rubrics_metrics.description: The series has gained a cult following and viewers have incorporated many of its quotes and in-jokes into daily use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term cultural penetration (quotability, in-jokes entering common use) is offered as evidence of legacy and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception and awards recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme was nominated for Best Situation Comedy at BAFTA twice, won the Audience Award at the British Academy Television Awards 2010 and won Outstanding Contribution to British Comedy at the British Comedy Awards 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry awards, nominations and positive critical scores (e.g., Metacritic score 73) are used as metrics of quality and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewership / ratings milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: The first episode of the third series had the highest-ever audience for an E4 original commission; series and episode viewer counts and audience share are tracked as indicators of popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcast ratings, record-breaking viewership numbers and time-shift viewers are presented as quantitative measures of the show's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode runtime and series length
rubrics_metrics.description: Running time: 22–25 minutes; number of series: 3; number of episodes: 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format and episode/runtime constraints are factual production standards that shape pacing and comedic structure for situational sitcoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music selection and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: The music was chosen by the music supervisor and then Xfm DJ Marsha Shandur; opening theme and featured artists are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curated soundtrack choices and a distinctive opening theme contribute to tone and identity; music supervision is presented as a deliberate creative element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content classification / certification considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: All DVDs received an 18 certificate in the UK and MA15+ in Australia due to their high quantity of strong language, crude humour and strong, frequent, sex references; the theatrical film received a 15 certificate (extended cut 18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content choices (language, sexual material, crude humour) directly affect age certification and distribution formats, which are practical constraints and considerations for producers and distributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin-offs, adaptations and international versions as success indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The Inbetweeners spawned films (The Inbetweeners Movie, The Inbetweeners 2) and an American adaptation (which was cancelled after one season).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions into films and international remakes are used as indicators of commercial success and cross-market appeal; the relative failure of the American version signals limits of cultural transferability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and platform availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Series available on Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Channel 4's All 4; international broadcast across multiple networks and home-media DVD/Blu-ray releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad platform availability and home-media releases are practical metrics of accessibility and commercial reach.
